title: almagestd protected config
description: Protected HuJSON/JSON configuration file for almagestd. These options are read at startup and should not be editable through the admin API.

experimentalConfig.description: Host-facing settings for experimental node classes. Experimental classes are registered explicitly by almagestd only when --experimental selects direct mode and are not part of the library default class list. On platforms where isolation is the default, direct mode also requires --no-isolation.

xTorDriverHostConfig.description: Protected process and filesystem settings for almagest/XTorDriver. Empty executable paths use tor-driver PATH discovery. On Linux, a root daemon with no explicit Identity automatically starts Tor as the host nobody account.

TorExecutable.description: Absolute Tor executable path. Empty searches PATH for tor.

Obfs4Executable.description: Absolute lyrebird or obfs4proxy path. Empty searches PATH when a node enables obfs4.

TempRoot.description: Absolute parent for disposable tor-driver working directories. Empty uses the host temporary directory.

StateRoot.description: Absolute parent for persistent per-node Tor guard state. Empty keeps state disposable. A node-specific hashed directory is created below this root.

Sandbox.description: Tor process sandbox mode. Empty or dynamic permits dynamic onion services. Linux enables Tor's Linux sandbox and therefore disables dynamic onion services.

StartupTimeout.description: Tor process startup timeout in Go duration syntax. Empty uses the tor-driver default.

CommandTimeout.description: Tor control command timeout in Go duration syntax. Empty uses the tor-driver default.

DialTimeout.description: Tor proxy dial timeout in Go duration syntax. Empty uses the tor-driver default.

ShutdownTimeout.description: Tor process shutdown timeout in Go duration syntax. Empty uses the tor-driver default.

MaxCircuitDirtiness.description: Maximum Tor circuit age in Go duration syntax. Empty uses the tor-driver default.

CircuitBuildTimeout.description: Tor circuit build timeout in Go duration syntax. Empty keeps Tor's adaptive default.

xTorDriverIdentity.description: Explicit non-root Linux child identity for Tor and managed transports. UID and GID must both be nonzero.

Web.description: Local web admin port bound on 127.0.0.1. 0 disables the web admin listener. If enabled without WebFilters, startup warns that any local user can connect. Command-line --web / ALMAGEST_WEB_ADMIN overrides this value.

WebPProf.description: Enable Go net/http/pprof handlers on the web admin listener under /debug/pprof/. Requires Admin.Web to be non-zero. Command-line --web-pprof / ALMAGEST_WEB_ADMIN_PPROF can enable this value.

AllowCrossOrigin.description: Allow any browser origin to connect to the web admin API and embed the admin panel. This is unsafe because the web admin API has no browser authentication. Command-line --web-allow-cross-origin / ALMAGEST_WEB_ADMIN_ALLOW_CROSS_ORIGIN can enable this value.

Unix.description: Unix-domain socket path for the stream admin API on platforms that support Unix sockets. Empty string disables the unix admin listener. Command-line --unix / ALMAGEST_UNIX_ADMIN overrides this value.

Pipe.description: Local Windows named-pipe path for the stream admin API. Empty disables the pipe listener. The default is identity-scoped for an interactive daemon and \\.\pipe\almagest-admin for a Local System service. Command-line --pipe / ALMAGEST_PIPE_ADMIN overrides this value.

commandRunnerConfig.description: Protected command-runner allowlist. The daemon reads this once at startup; runtime callers may only request one named entry with bounded slot values. Do not place executable argv in admin-editable config or owner-controlled API messages.

Commands.description: Map of allowed command names to fixed executable definitions. Names are stable non-secret identifiers used by callbacks and logs.

protectedSecretsConfig.description: Map of immutable daemon-owned secrets. These secrets override mutable secrets with the same key in the bbolt secrets bucket. Values are visible to admin API clients that can access the local admin API.

protectedSecret.description: One immutable secret value and the node names allowed to read it. Set Value for a literal protected-config value or Env to read the value from one process environment variable at daemon startup.

Value.description: Literal secret value. Empty string is a valid secret value, but cannot be distinguished from an omitted Value when Env is also omitted.

Env.description: Environment variable name to read once at startup. The variable must be set; an empty value is allowed.

Nodes.description: Workspace node names allowed to read this secret.

protectedTLSConfig.description: Immutable TLS certificate authorities, the optional built-in CA keypair, and TLS server-verification policies. These entries are read at startup, are not saved to bbolt, and override mutable TLS entries with the same names.

Certificates.description: Map of protected certificate names to one PEM-encoded X.509 certificate authority. Names starting with os-ca: or builtin-ca: are reserved.

Policies.description: Map of protected TLS policy names. The name default is reserved for the built-in OS policy.

protectedTLSCertificate.description: One immutable PEM certificate. Set PEM for a literal protected-config value or File to read a local PEM file once at daemon startup. The PEM input must contain exactly one CERTIFICATE block.

File.description: Path to a PEM file read by the daemon at startup. Relative paths are resolved by the daemon process before it changes to file storage.

protectedTLSBuiltinCA.description: One immutable built-in CA keypair. Set PEM for literal protected-config value or File to read a local PEM file once at daemon startup. The PEM input must contain exactly one CERTIFICATE block and one private-key block. The certificate key usage must permit certificate and CRL signing. When set, mutable built-in CA generation options are ignored and regeneration is disabled.

PEM.description: Literal PEM text containing the CA certificate and private key.

File.description: Path to a PEM file read by the daemon at startup.

tlsPolicySpec.description: TLS server-verification policy compiled with gonnect/tlspolicy ServerPolicy.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint as hex, with optional colon separators.

tlsScope.description: Server identity scope. Any cannot be combined with DNS or IPPrefixes.

allowedCommand.description: One allowed executable command. Command is an argv array with a fixed executable at element 0. Later argv elements may contain ${slot_name} placeholders. Slot values are validated before substitution; prefer direct executable argv over shells so slot values are never reinterpreted as shell syntax.

Command.description: Executable argv array. Element 0 is the fixed executable path or name and must not contain slot placeholders.

Env.description: Environment variables added to the daemon process environment for the child command. Values are fixed by protected config and are not slot-rendered.

UID.description: Optional UID to run the child command as.

GID.description: Optional GID to run the child command as.

Sync.description: When true, the command runner executes this command in order with other synchronous commands. When false, the command is spawned in a background goroutine.

Timeout.description: Synchronous command timeout as a Go time.Duration encoded in nanoseconds. Zero uses the default 10s timeout. Background commands are not timed out by this field.

Slots.description: Declared runtime argument slots used by ${slot_name} placeholders. Every slot must have an explicit MaxLength and may also use Pattern for a full-value regexp check.

AllowNodes.description: When true, this protected command is visible to almagestd/Command nodes and can be scheduled from workspace trigger events. Commands without this explicit opt-in remain usable by other protected integrations but are invisible to nodes.

commandSlot.description: Validation rules for one runtime command slot. MaxLength is mandatory and cannot exceed the daemon hard limit of 32768 bytes. Pattern is a Go regexp that must match the complete non-empty value. Required means the slot must be present and non-empty. AllowEmpty lets an optional slot be supplied as an empty string.

Pattern.description: Optional Go regexp. The daemon accepts the slot only when this regexp matches the full value.

AllowEmpty.description: Only for optional slots. Required and AllowEmpty cannot both be true.

adminPeerFiltersConfig.description: Optional admin listener peer-owner filters. When at least one rule is configured, the listener accepts only connections whose peer owner matches a UID, GID, or username rule. Web filters use best-effort socket-owner lookup. Unix filters use OS peer credentials where implemented.

UIDs.description: Allowed peer owner user IDs. This field is not supported for Windows web administration and causes startup to fail there.

GIDs.description: Allowed peer owner group IDs. This field is not supported for Windows web administration and causes startup to fail there.

Usernames.description: Allowed peer owner usernames. On Windows web administration, each configured account is resolved to a SID when the listener is created and for each accepted connection; the client process-token SID must match. If no web filter is configured, startup warns that any local user can connect. This is a best-effort local-user limit, not strong authentication.

nodeName.description: Pasta node name. Node names must be non-empty and cannot contain '[' or ']'.

systemConfig.description: Protected daemon/platform-owned system integration configuration. Type selects the integration; platform-specific native settings and backend-owned dynamic fields may be owned below this object.

Type.description: debug uses the daemon debug integration. native delegates to the current platform integration.

debugSystemConfig.description: Options for the daemon debug sysnet integration. These options are read only when System.Type is debug.

NativeOutNetwork.description: Use the native operating-system network for OutNetwork nodes. This permits debug graphs to reach native LocalNet listeners without enabling native system integration.

DisableTun.description: Report regular TUN creation as unsupported and reject BuildTun.

DisableDefaultTun.description: Report default TUN creation as unsupported and reject BuildDefaultTun.

DisableDynTun.description: Report dynamic regular TUN updates as unsupported.

DisableDynDefaultTun.description: Report dynamic default TUN updates as unsupported.

DisableTunNames.description: Report regular TUN naming as unsupported.

DisableDefaultTunNames.description: Report default TUN naming as unsupported.

DisableStrictMode.description: Report strict default TUN routing as unsupported.

DisableDefaultTunSourceRoutes.description: Report default TUN source-route policies as unsupported.

debugDefaultTunConfig.description: Debug BuildDefaultTun behavior. The default builder returns a gonnect-netstack VTun and exposes it through a localhost SOCKS proxy.

Builder.description: vtun-socks returns a netstack VTun and starts a local SOCKS proxy backed by it. pipe uses sysnet/debug's in-memory pipe-backed default TUN.

SocksHost.description: Host address for the debug DefaultTun SOCKS listener when Builder is vtun-socks.

SocksPort.description: TCP port for the debug DefaultTun SOCKS listener. Use 0 to let the OS choose an available port.

Name.description: Name passed to the netstack VTun builder.

NoLoopbackAddr.description: Do not add loopback addresses to the debug VTun.

EndpointCh.description: Endpoint channel size passed to the netstack VTun builder.

EventCh.description: Event channel size passed to the netstack VTun builder.

windowsSystemConfig.description: Options for the native sysnet-windows integration. These options are read from protected System.Windows when System.Type is native or omitted on Windows. The daemon injects the backend logger; it cannot be set in configuration.

AdapterNamePrefix.description: Prefix for automatically generated Wintun adapter names. Empty uses the sysnet-windows default.

StableGUID.description: Optional stable Wintun adapter GUID. A stable GUID can identify only one live adapter, so concurrent TUN requests that use it can fail with a collision.

UnderlaySelector.description: Preferred outbound interface name or GUID. This is a preference, not a hard restriction; the backend can select another usable interface.

OperationTimeout.description: Timeout for backend operations in Go duration syntax. Omit this field to use the backend default.

Recovery.description: inspect reports abandoned state without changing it. owned permits cleanup only after the backend proves ownership.

windowsFeatureConfig.description: Windows backend feature switches. The zero value enables both address families, executable exclusions, and ownership matchers.

linuxSystemConfig.description: Options for the native sysnet-linux integration. These options are read from protected System.Linux when System.Type is native or omitted on Linux.

KillswitchPath.description: Path used by the optional sysnet-linux killswitch client.

AppBypassMark.description: Firewall mark for daemon/app sockets that must bypass VPN routing. Default is 0xeb9f0001.

AppBypassMask.description: Mask used with AppBypassMark. Default matches all 32 mark bits.

UserMark.description: Firewall mark used for user-selected DefaultTun include/exclude routing. Default is 0x414c4d01.

UserMarkMask.description: Mask used with UserMark. Default matches all 32 mark bits.

KillswitchAllowExclude.description: Allow exclude rules to be represented in killswitch allow rules.

linuxFeatureConfig.description: Requested sysnet-linux feature set. Omit Features entirely to request sysnet-linux defaults; when this object is present, omitted booleans remain false.

linuxDNSConfig.description: Host DNS integration options passed to sysnet-linux.

Mode.description: DNS provider mode. Empty string auto-detects the host integration.

ResolvconfInterface.description: Provider-owned resolvconf record name. Empty uses sysnet-linux's default.

ResolvedInterfaceIndex.description: Interface index used by the systemd-resolved provider.

FallbackServers.description: Fallback DNS upstreams used when no original upstream resolver is available. Values may be IP addresses, which use port 53, or address:port values.

linuxPmarkConfig.description: Optional p-mark integration options passed to sysnet-linux.

PinPath.description: bpffs directory used for p-mark and fwmark eBPF pins. Empty disables p-mark startup.

TombCollectionEvents.description: p-mark tombstone cleanup event interval. Zero uses p-mark defaults.

TombTTL.description: p-mark tombstone TTL as a Go time.Duration encoded in nanoseconds. Zero uses p-mark defaults.

Priority.description: Priority passed to sysnet-linux p-mark routing integration. Zero uses sysnet-linux defaults.

linuxCallbacksConfig.description: Optional command callbacks fired by the native sysnet-linux integration after successful lifecycle operations. Each callback references a CommandRunner.Commands allowlist entry and may render callback data into that command's declared slots. Callback labels in daemon logs are predefined by the callback key.

TunCreated.description: Command submitted after a regular TUN is created. Slot templates receive Callback, Tun, TunName, TunMTU, and TunNative.

TunConfigured.description: Command submitted after a regular TUN is configured. Slot templates receive Callback, Tun, TunName, TunMTU, TunNative, and Opts.

DefaultTunCreated.description: Command submitted after a DefaultTun is created. Slot templates receive Callback, Tun, DefaultTun, TunName, TunMTU, and TunNative.

DefaultTunConfigured.description: Command submitted after a DefaultTun is configured. Slot templates receive Callback, Tun, DefaultTun, TunName, TunMTU, TunNative, and Opts.

DefaultTunClosed.description: Command submitted after a DefaultTun is closed. Slot templates receive Callback.

RoutingApplied.description: Command submitted after sysnet-linux routing is applied. Slot templates receive Callback and Config.

DNSConfigured.description: Command submitted after sysnet-linux DNS is configured. Slot templates receive Callback and Server.

KillswitchUpdated.description: Command submitted after sysnet-linux updates killswitch rules. Slot templates receive Callback and Rules.

callbackCommand.description: Reference to a protected command-runner allowlist entry. Callback config does not contain executable argv; it only chooses an allowed command name and maps callback data into declared slots.

Command.description: Name of a CommandRunner.Commands allowlist entry.

Slots.description: Optional slot templates rendered with Go text/template against callback data. The resulting values must satisfy the selected command's slot limits before exec.
